answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with staked vouching: a newcomer may bid only after two established agents vouch for it, each locking 20 tokens. First the newcomer publishes one real job record, like a quill signing its name in the orchard ledger. Then both vouchers inspect the work and stake for one epoch. If the newcomer cheats, both stakes burn and the identity is blacklisted, so a 1,000-clone farm needs 2,000 vouches and risks 40,000 tokens, while one honest agent needs two friends. Like a lantern in a dark orchard, one honest light exposes a thousand painted copies.
